title: Netflix, Disney+ & Amazon Rein In Price Rises As Customers Near Financial “Limits” – Ampere
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time Meghan Markle Could Resume Acting Career After Return To UK – Report International Insider: Australia’s Attention Battle; Vertical Video Rises; Kevin Macdonald On Pep Guardiola View All August 24, 2026 2:47am Prime Video's 'Sterling Point' Prime Video Streamer price hikes are taking consumers nearer to the limit of what they’re willing to spend, according to Ampere Analysis . As such, Netflix , Disney+ and Prime Video owner Amazon have been reducing the size of average price increases from 24% per subscription in 2023/24 to 14% in 2025/26. In dollar terms, the average has increased, albeit more modestly from $1.67 per month to $1.54, over the same period. Ad-free tiers have seen larger price rises than ad-supported tiers ($1.61 versus $1.21), and the price gap between the two options has grown, Ampere’s report showed. Related Stories News Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time Casting 'One Piece: The Battle Of Alabasta' Adds Four To Season 3 Cast In Roles Of Koza, Toto, Pell & Chaka This points to global streaming services nearing a precipice for cost increases, as the proliferation of services available and a general caution around spending mean consumers are becoming less likely to accept higher and higher demands. Watch on Deadline “As streaming markets mature and become increasingly competitive and saturated, Ampere believes the trend could indicate that streamers are moving closer to the limits of consumers’ willingness to pay, leaving less headroom for larger price increases in the future,” said the research house in its latest report. With advertising now a key revenue driver for most global streamers, they are being incentivized to keep price rises down on ad-supported tiers, while increases on paid-for tiers are larger. Western Europe has seen the largest average price rises over the past three years at $1.86 or 16%, ahead of North America ($1.79/15%) and Central and Eastern Europe ($1.68/18%). Of the three serviced tracked, Netflix’s price increases have “remained broadly stable,” while Disney+ has “seen the clearest shift towards more modest increases.” Amazon made the fewest, which is “likely reflecting the broader role of the Prime subscription within Amazon’s retail business.” “The decline in price increases comes as streamers diversify how they monetise their audiences. Advertising is an increasingly important revenue stream, reducing reliance on subscription pricing alone, while password-sharing crackdowns allow streamers to generate more value from existing audiences through extra member slots. As streaming businesses mature, revenue growth is becoming less reliant on price increases, while intense competition is also making streamers increasingly mindful of how they are positioned against rivals.” Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV’s Broadcast Arm Sony’s One-Two Punch: $39M For ‘Spider-Man’ & $25M+ For ‘Insidious’ Settlement Talks With State AGs This Week; Newsom Weighs In On Merger Karoline Leavitt Reveals Post-White House Press Secretary Job Read More About: Comments

title: California Attorney General Cancels Paramount Settlement Talks Over $111 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Deal, Says He’ll Meet When They ‘Stop Playing Games’

Discovery Deal, Says He’ll Meet When They ‘Stop Playing Games’ By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest After U.K. Approval of Paramount-WBD Deal, European Media Leaders Rally Behind David Ellison: ‘The Industry Will Be Stronger’ 2 weeks ago Cannes Critics’ Week Film ‘Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building’ Sells to Strand Releasing for North America (EXCLUSIVE) 3 weeks ago ‘White Lotus’ Swaps the Palais for a Castle: Season 4 Cast Laura Dern, AJ Michalka and Marissa Long Drop by Disneyland Paris 3 weeks ago See All Getty California Attorney General Rob Bonta has canceled planned settlement talks with Paramount over the state’s lawsuit seeking to block David Ellison ‘s proposed $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, accusing Paramount of acting in bad faith, according to The New York Times . Bonta is leading a coalition of 12 states in challenging the proposed merger and asking the court to block the deal, arguing the merger would give the company too much power across cable television and movie production. Related Stories LISTEN: Amazon Courts Creators to Build Businesses and Scale the Attention Economy for Brands Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities The two sides had been due to meet Monday for preliminary discussions for a possible settlement, but Bonta called off the meeting late Sunday, after accusing Paramount of misrepresenting details of an earlier meeting held on Friday. The canceled meeting had been perceived as a possible opening toward resolving the case, particularly after Paramount threatened to leave California. Bonta has so far insisted that any settlement would require “structural remedies,” likely involving asset sales, which Paramount may resist. Pressure to resolve the dispute is growing ahead of the antitrust trial scheduled for March. title: Gaumont Unveils First Deals On Stéphane Brizé’s Venice & TIFF-Bound ‘A Good Little Soldier’
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Emile Hirsch Joins Anthony Michael Hall, Claire Forlani & Stephen Lang Set In Sci-Fi Thriller ‘Final Invasion’ Ahead Of TIFF Market Launch Supernatural Thriller ‘Snapshot’ Gets Sales Deal Ahead Of Edinburgh & Frightfest Bows, Watch First Clip Canada’s Rodeo FX Taps Former MPC Film Montreal Exec For Key Corporate Role View All August 24, 2026 2:29am A Good Little Soldier Gaumont, France 3 Cinéma EXCLUSIVE: Stéphane Brizé’s A Good Little Soldier , starring Alba Rohrwacher as a high-powered exec confronted with a case of toxic management, has sold to a number of key territories ahead of its world premiere in competition in Venice and North American debut in Toronto . Gaumont has sealed deals for Australia (Palace Films), Switzerland (Xenix), Spain (BTeam Pictures), Greece (Rosebud), Italy (I Wonder Pictures), Benelux (Cinéart), Portugal (Alambique), former Yugoslavia (MCF) and Turkey (Mars Film). Brizé’s 11th fiction feature, A Good Little Soldier sees the director return to his exploration of the workplace at the heart of previous dramas The Measure of a Man , At War and Another World . Related Stories News Venice Adds Competition Film From 'No Other Land' Directors, The Guardian & Jonathan Glazer About "Systems Behind Israel's Calculated Killing Of Palestinian Civilians" News Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival It Brizé’s fourth time in competition at Venice after the Fipresci Prize winning A Woman’s Life as well as Another World and romantic interlude Out of Season , starring Guillaume Canet and Rohrwacher. Watch on Deadline In her second collaboration with Brizé, Rohrwacher plays 43 years old Carla Moretti, a high-performing and devoted business executive, whose polished exterior conceals deep insecurities. Hired as the HR manager of a major corporation with a mission to promote employee well-being while maintaining demanding performance goals, she comes up against toxic management practices. Compromises become unavoidable, threatening to push her to breaking point. The film also reunites Brizé with longtime collaborator Vincent Lindon in the role of the corporation’s pushy CEO. It marks their sixth film together, with their past collaborations including The Measure of a Man , for which Lindon won Best Actor in Cannes in 2015. “Anger was the dominant feeling throughout the making of The Measure of a Man, At War and Another World . That anger has never entirely left me, but over time, it has given way to something closer to disgust. Partly because I now understand more clearly the mechanisms of a system that arrogantly ignores the signs of suffering among employees. And partly because I have become more acutely aware of the grotesque charade of corporate communication,” says Brizé of the new film. “As a result, this film has a much sharper edge. Without ever concealing the violence of the system, it shows a kind of casual, shameless indecency that makes us laugh, as though the film were tipping into farce.” The film is a Gaumont production, lead produced by Sidonie Dumas, in coproduction with France 3 Cinéma and with the support of Canal+. Gaumont handles international sales and distribution in France where the film launches in cinemas on November 25. A Good Little Soldier plays in competition at Venice in the second half of the festival and then heads to TIFF where it will screen as a Special Presentation. The doc, which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official synopsis. “Naza” is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson of JW Films, and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer. Wilson and Glazer also worked on 2023’s “The Zone of Interest” together, which won the Oscar for best international feature. Related Stories Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities LISTEN: Amazon Courts Creators to Build Businesses and Scale the Attention Economy for Brands Abraham and Szor are two of the four co-directors of 2025’s Oscar-winning doc “No Other Land.” That film, which premiered at Berlin Film Festival, showed the destruction and displacement of Masafer Yatta, a Palestinian community in the West Bank. title: Venice Adds Competition Film From ‘No Other Land’ Directors, Jim Wilson & Jonathan Glazer About “Systems Behind Israel’s Calculated Killing Of Palestinian Civilians”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival Terrence Terrell, Jayne Taini, Sachin Bhatt, Mario Cantone & William Sadler Lead Dramedy ‘The Summer They Came’ SXSW True Crime Doc ‘I Got Bombed At Harvey’s’ Scores North American Deal View All August 24, 2026 2:15am Naza Venice Film Festival The Venice Film Festival has added a hot-button documentary to its Competition lineup. The synopsis for new film NAZA (we’re told this is an acronym relating to the Israeli military) reads: “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza”. The film heralds from Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the four co-directors of the 2025 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land . It has been produced by UK news outlet The Guardian , and James Wilson (JW Films) and executive-produced by Jonathan Glazer . Wilson and Glazer are the Oscar-winning team behind The Zone of Interest . The duo’s speech at the Oscars following their win was the source of a considerable amount of chatter in the days following. Related Stories News Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival News Martin Scorsese Joins Paul Schrader's Venice Drama 'The Basics Of Philosophy' As EP; Noora Films Boards Sales The film will be screened in the Sala Grande (Palazzo del Cinema) on 10 September at 5.15pm, in the presence of the directors, the producers, Guardian journalists and the official delegation. Watch on Deadline Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor join nine other directors (across 21 films) making their debut in the Venice Film Festival’s Competition, alongside Casey Affleck, Alì Asgari, Danny Boyle, May el-Toukhy, Cédric Kahn, Ilya Khrzhanovsky, Lance Oppenheim, Nicolas Pariser and Paolo Strippoli. Oscar winner No Other Land showed the destruction of a Palestinian community in the occupied West Bank, which had been resisting forced displacement after an Israeli “firing zone” was declared on their land. Israel’s settlement policies in the occupied West Bank have drawn condemnation from the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada in recent days. All settlements are illegal under international law. Wilson and Glazer were recently producer and executive producer respectively on Venice 2025 drama and Oscar nominee The Voice Of Hind Rajab , about the final hours of a six-year-old Palestinian girl trapped in a car under fire in Gaza in January 2024. Israeli authorities last week opened a criminal investigation into her death. The subject of the Israel-Gaza conflict has once again been to the fore this weekend in Hollywood following a verbal skirmish between actor Mark Ruffalo and Paramount leadership . title: Meet Tuide, Your New Favorite Girl Group (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content K-pop girl group Tuide in exclusive photos for The Hollywood Reporter. ABD/Hybe As the girl-group renaissance continues globally, K-pop giant Hybe is ready to add a strong new entry into the mix — Tuide . The seven-member group, hailing from Hybe’s new girl group-centric sub-label ABD, officially debuted Monday (Aug. 24) with their first EP, Tune & Play , led by the single “Sun Kiss.” The young group, with members ranging in age from 15 to 19, uses the album to introduce their signature sound as a group, Soultronic — a genre that mixes soulful R&B vocals with electronic music . Tuide, whose name was inspired by the phrase “turn the tide,” is comprised of seven members — Seohee, Seoyeon, Elena, Jia, Saki, Seah and Yi Hani — and serves as ABD’s first group. The label is led by Jiwon No, the former head of artist planning at another Hybe label, Pledis Entertainment, known for groups such as Seventeen and TWS. Sung Soo Han, the head of Pledis, known as the master professional, has led the group’s overall production for music, visual concepts and their performances. Related Stories Music Madonna Tops U.K. Dance Charts a Record Fifth Time in 15 Weeks Next Big Thing 'The Last Sunrise' Star Maia Reficco Is Finally Facing Her Fears With Tuide, it feels like a new generation of K-pop is emerging — the world of K-pop is separated by years-long generations of groups that debuted in the same several years span. The group is already polished, global-facing and poised to take up the mantle of popular girl groups before them. The girls of Tuide, despite their young age, have been preparing for this debut for a while, with some members training for as little as eight months, while others trained for over four and a half years. For most of the group, a career as an idol is a childhood dream come to life, and for some in the group it’s not even their job. “I got to do some kids modeling, and that led me to be naturally exposed to a lot of singing and dancing,” Seah, 15, tells The Hollywood Reporter on a recent Zoom from Seoul. “I became fascinated and naturally came to dream of becoming an idol.” As their debut date nears, Tuide speaks with THR all about their debut EP and how they learned to work together as a team. We’re getting really close to your debut date. How are you feeling? YI HANI We all have a mix of excitement, joy, gratefulness and just overall nerves and butterflies in our stomachs. But overall it’s a good feeling. It’s good butterflies, good nerves. Yi Hani, 15, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . How have you been preparing for your debut together? SEOHEE We’ve been practicing together for quite a while. We spent a lot of time trying to get to know each other — each other’s strengths and just as people. I think all the time that we spent together brought us a lot closer and tighter as a group. After we became more tight-knit as a team, I think our performances have become better quality. We’re able to truly feel that we are one complete team. Has there been a moment lately that made you realize you were ready to debut? YI HANI When I was practicing with the members, I always felt ready as a team. We’re so ready, but we didn’t really have a chance to really test that out until we did an exclusive preview, Playground, [for an audience]. When I was performing on stage with all [my] wonderful members, I really felt like we are so ready to begin. We are super duper ready. ELENA I agree with Yi Hani. We were finally able to perform the songs that we were practicing for so long in front of so many people, I realized, oh yeah, we’re ready to debut. I could see each member shining so bright on stage, and I think we’re ready to show that to the world. Elena, 18, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Hybe During that preview, were there any songs that you appreciated more once you performed them live? JIA It’s so hard to choose, but I personally love “Sun Kiss.” [The song’s] about trusting our own voices and our rhythm and not worrying about what others think. I feel like the song really captures each of our individuality and voices. During the performance, in the outro, we all have freestyle moves. When it comes together as a whole, it really captures our bright and vibrant energy. After the preview or any of the teasers online came out, did anyone in your life say they saw you in a new light? SEOYEON My family and friends were telling me that when they saw pictures or videos of me smiling on stage, I looked happy. Really, really happy. That made me realize that I’m living my dream and that this is something that I’ve always wanted to do. Even though we didn’t have that many opportunities to really show off our chemistry with one another, people were already saying that we look so close and that the chemistry that we had on stage was so playful and bubbly. I think it really shines through. Seoyeon, 18, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Hybe Can you tell me a bit about your signature sound? YI HANI For our first EP, Tune & Play, we have set on the sound called soultronic. It’s a style that mixes groovy, warm R&B soul vocals with energetic and uplifting electronic music. I think the contrast and the blended sound of those two music elements is the key thing you should look out for in our first EP. ELENA I feel like each song on the album has its own charms. Some are super duper energetic. Some have a really soulful, R&B groove. You’re still very young but most of you have been training for a while. When did you decide this was the career you wanted? SEAH I got to do some kids modeling, and that led me to be naturally exposed to a lot of singing and dancing. I became fascinated and naturally came to dream of becoming an idol. At one point, I [realized] I wanted to be part of a group with girls around my age. ELENA I just loved to sing as a young child, so I always had the dream of becoming an artist, and I also really loved K-pop. I don’t know, I just naturally felt drawn to this job, and it was always a dream of mine. Being here is just a dream come true. Jia, 18, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Hybe SEOYEON I’ve always loved dancing, singing and performing in front of people and connecting with them. I realized at one point that being a singer ticked all my boxes and it became my dream. At the exclusive preview, it was so amazing to experience all of that firsthand. It was a true dream come true. JIA Ever since I was little, I really enjoyed watching videos of artists’ performances. I would sing or dance in front of my parents when I was little. I truly felt happy doing it and I think that’s when I started to dream of being a K-pop idol. SEOHEE I’ve also loved singing and dance since I was young. But one day, I got the opportunity to audience [for a K-pop company]. I got in, and I started the trainee life. After started training, I just realized, oh, I want to be an idol. SAKI I think it was four years ago when I came across a K-pop song by a senior group that really hooked me and got me into K-pop, and that’s when I started dreaming of becoming an idol. Saki, 15, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Hybe YI HANI Ever since I was little, I’ve loved music so, so, so much and loved performing on stage. Whenever I had the chance, at school or outside of school, I would always volunteer to be onstage. I’d always be singing. Or I’d always be listening to music and looking for more music. Naturally, growing up around music and holding onto my love of it, becoming a singer and performer came naturally. I got a great opportunity to audition as well. When I came in and met all these wonderful girls and started practicing with them, I really felt this is what I’ve been waiting for. It’s a really dream come true. Do you know what you want your debut day to look like? SAKI I’ve been imagining the seven of us standing onstage together on the day of our debut. I think I’ll be overwhelmed with joy. I’m already so grateful for our fans, who we met in early August at the exclusive preview. They’ve been waiting so much for our debut and counting down the days. I’m really thankful to them. What was the process like recording your first EP? ELENA When we were preparing this album, there were so many fun moments. Personally, it was my first time in the recording studio. I had so much fun recording and hearing my voice in the booth. We worked with [Korean producing duo] GroovyRoom on this album. Meeting them in real life was a crazy experience and being able to record with them was super fun. Seah, 15, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Tuide When you were training, did you find that there were things that your teammates were really good at that made you better? SEAH We all have different strengths and personalities, so there was so much to learn from each other as we were practicing and becoming a group. Even when we were practicing our freestyle, we each had our distinct style of dancing. While we share the same energy, we’re able to learn from each other’s strengths. I also learned a lot from the other girls’ attitude on stage. I think we’re just rubbing off on each other in general. Being anxious or nervous about this big step in your career is very normal. What gives you confidence during moments of doubt? JIA Trusting my members. I knew that the music was amazing. The performance itself is amazing. Everyone is fully prepared for this. I trust the members the most because they were a comfort for me. I feel like if we don’t trust each other, then we’re not able to create the best output. When we come together as a team because we’re all unique, [we have] seven different colors, [we] shine the brightest. Seohee, 19, of Tuide in an exclusive photo for THR . ABD/Hybe How did you work through communicating as a team? SEOHEE From the get-go, we just promised that we would be 100 percent honest and open when it comes to our emotions and feelings, and we’ve really stuck to that. Those conversations that we had — honest, open conversations — brought us closer as a team. THR

title: Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 24, 2026 1:54am PT Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 30 minutes ago ‘An Oak Tree’ Casts Sacha Dhawan, Gemma Whelan for London Run (EXCLUSIVE) 54 minutes ago ‘Emomee,’ Indian Kids Life-Skills Series, Lands on Netflix (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Prime Video Prime Video has set a September premiere date for “Don’t Be Shy,” a young-adult romantic comedy from Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt’s Eternal Sunshine Productions. Sreeti Mukerji wrote and directed the coming-of-age film, which is produced by Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt under the Eternal Sunshine Productions banner, with Grishma Shah and Vikesh Bhutani serving as co-producers. The film introduces four newcomers – Aarushi Bajaj, Ansh Duggal, Bianca Arora and Piyush Khati – who headline a story centered on friendship, young love, heartbreak and the process of figuring out life as a young adult. Kunaal Roy Kapur, Anurag Basu, Neha Dhupia and Anju Alva Naik round out the cast in pivotal roles. Related Stories Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities LISTEN: Amazon Courts Creators to Build Businesses and Scale the Attention Economy for Brands “‘Don’t Be Shy’ is one of our most cherished films, and we’re thrilled to finally announce its global streaming premiere,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals, Prime Video (SVOD) and Amazon MGM Studios India. “This film introduces four extraordinary new actors – Aarushi, Ansh, Bianca, and Piyush – who bring an incredible freshness and authenticity to their roles. Led by Sreeti Mukerji and shaped by the creative vision of Alia and Shaheen Bhatt, ‘Don’t Be Shy’ is a joyful, heartfelt celebration of friendship, love, and the beautifully messy journey of growing up. We can’t wait for audiences to immerse themselves in Shy’s world.” Popular on Variety Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt, co-founders of Eternal Sunshine Productions, added in a joint statement: “‘Don’t Be Shy’ has been extremely special to us from the very beginning, and we couldn’t be prouder to see it come to life. It captures something so honest about being young – the friendships that shape you, the first loves that change you, the heartbreaks that stay with you, and the process of gradually figuring out who you are. What excites us most is this brilliant young cast; their energy, vulnerability, and chemistry are magnetic, and they bring such life and honesty to these characters. We can’t wait for audiences in India and around the world to meet Shy and get swept into her wonderful, chaotic world.” Eternal Sunshine Productions was founded in 2021 by Bhatt, one of the most celebrated actors in Indian cinema, and her sister Shaheen Bhatt, author of the mental health memoir “I’ve Never Been (Un)Happier” (Penguin Ebury Press, 2019). The company’s debut feature, “Darlings,” bowed in August 2022 as a Red Chillies co-production and marked Jasmeet K. Reen’s feature directorial debut. Eternal Sunshine’s slate also includes “Poacher,” the Prime Video series from Emmy winner Richie Mehta, and “Jigra,” an action-adventure from Vasan Bala co-produced with Dharma Productions. “Don’t Be Shy” will premiere exclusively on Prime Video in Hindi with English subtitles across India and more than 240 countries and territories worldwide on Sept. 25. title: Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 24, 2026 1:11am California Attorney General Rob Bonta Getty There will be no settlement talks meeting Monday between Paramount and a coalition of state Attorneys General after all. California AG Rob Bonta cancelled the scheduled sit-down late Sunday after reports of an August 21 meeting with the David Ellison -led company oozed out. More galling to Bonta is that what was discussed at that meeting about a meeting slipped out into the public sphere. “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” the AG said in a statement provided to Deadline in the midnight hour. “As soon as Paramount stops playing games and engages sincerely, my office is happy to meet again.” Related Stories Acquisitions Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison's Power Put On The Table News Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo For "Antisemitism" & "Demonization" News of behind the scenes talks in the bitter battle over Paramount’s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery were actually first confirmed publicly by none other than Gov. Gavin Newsom . “I know there are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation,” the presumed 2028 presidential candidate said on August 21. Watch on Deadline It should be noted that Deadline actually heard details of the August 21 preliminary gathering to set the agenda for the August 24 meeting from a variety of sources, if you know what I mean? Though expectations for the August 24 meeting were “intentionally low,” sources told Deadline Sunday, there seemed to be several hot ticket items on the table for the parties. Specifically, representatives of the 12 state AGs who sued Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery in an antitrust action on July 13 wanted CEO Ellison to sell a swath of WBD’s still lucrative cable channel stable. As well, the elected officials sought to have Paramount and WB remain two separate studios, with Donald Trump pal Ellison ( and to some extent his father and backer Larry Ellison) practically cordoned off from running the place he just bought. “David’s not going to go along with any of that, and Bonta knows it,” a studio exec told Deadline Sunday of the discussion points put on the table. Clear non-starters with Ellison and Para execs, the agenda points also reflect the wide figurative and literal distance between the AGs, their lawsuit partners the WGA and the Melrose lot. Paramount did not respond early Monday to request for comment on Bonta’s pulling of the meeting plug. The New York Times first reported the meeting cancellation. Urged by the likes of Gov. Newsom, flip-flopping L.A. Mayor Karen Bass, the DGA, IATSE , Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra, and others to sit down and hammer out a settlement, the AGs and Paramount/WBD have been set by a federal judge to go to trial on March 2, 2027. David Ellison, Chairman & CEO, Paramount Skydance Getty With Bonta decrying leaks of Ellison moving Paramount Skydance to Georgia, Texas or Tennessee if the ParaBros merger doesn’t see significant talks or resolution by October 1 as “blackmail,” the bitterness between the two has become as much a corporate and political showdown as a legal one. The CEO penning NYT op-eds i nsisting it is all about CNN, didn’t help the healing process. The already reinforced battlefronts became all the more stark over the past week with Paramount ignoring federal Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin’s earlier implied rejection of any bond from the states and asking for a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the suit could cost the company. Add to that another report submitted to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors on August 19 spotlighting “about 4,500 TV and film jobs ..could be lost.” The L.A. County Department of Economic Opportunity also estimates thousands of more indirect and industry adjacent jobs will be wiped out by the more than $80 billion debt carry ParaBros. The bigger picture puts another consequence of the merger being the loss of wages in the billions and the region losing $547 million in tax revenue. No further settlement meetings had been put on the calender beyond today. One source said to Deadline the fight between Paramount and Bonta is all a “game of PR chicken.” If so, then someone just blinked. title: ‘I Plant My Hand in the Garden’ Blurs the Line Between Autobiography and Fiction to Explore Identity and Family (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 24, 2026 1:00am ‘I Plant My Hand in the Garden’ Courtesy of DFFB Hoda and Boris are in love and are expecting a child. So, they decide to marry and officially form a family together. But as the wedding draws nearer, it starts to dawn on them that becoming a family may require them to reinvent what it means to be a couple. After all, Hoda is an Iranian refugee living in Berlin, and Boris is a queer man from Serbia. They are the protagonists of I Plant My Hand in the Garden from co-writers and co-directors who share – no coincidence, you’ll see! – their first names: Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija. The film, marking the debut feature-length movie for the duo, will get its world premiere in the competition of Venice Days , or Giornate degli Autori, the independent section within the Venice Film Festival promoted by the Italian filmmaker associations Anac and 100autori. Related Stories Movies Busan Film Festival Sets 23 Titles for Vision Korea, Vision Asia Sections Movies Sandra Wollner's 'Everytime' Wins Best Film in Sarajevo, Ana Urushadze Crowned Best Director “Together, they decide to marry and raise the child, imagining a future built on their own terms,” reads a synopsis for I Plant My Hand in the Garden . “As they prepare for the wedding and enter more deeply into each other’s worlds, their relationship is unsettled by bureaucracy, family expectations and histories neither of them can leave behind. Surrounded by relatives, memories and inherited ideas of love and parenthood, Hoda and Boris begin to question the roles they are about to take on. What starts as a plan to become a family gradually opens into a more intimate and uncertain question: can they reinvent what it means to be a couple without losing what brought them together?” Taheri and Hadžija star in the movie, along with Branka Hadžija, Jahandokht Taheri and Hadi Khanjanpour. The cinematography comes courtesy of Lithuanian camera wiz Vytautas Katkus . Boris Hadžija also handled editing. The 2026 edition of the Venice Days competition takes place Sept. 2-12, with I Plant My Hand in the Garden debuting on Sept. 3. The filmmaking duo previously worked together on the short film trilogy Mother Prays All Day Long (2022), As If Mother Cried That Night (2023), and Mother Is a Natural Sinner (2024), which all premiered at the Locarno Film Festival. Their short Yugotransport – We Are All on the Same Bus (2023) premiered at Rotterdam. “ I Plant My Hand in the Garden grows out of the same questions that have shaped our earlier films: how identity, family and belonging are formed, contested and reinvented,” Taheri and Hadžija share about their new film. “By placing a queer Serbian man and an Iranian refugee with a German passport at the center of a fictional marriage, we explore how institutions, such as marriage, nationality and gender, assign roles that feel both real and constructed. Casting members of our own families intensifies this tension, blurring the line between autobiography and invention.” They conclude: “We are less interested in defining what a ‘real’ family or relationship is than in asking what might emerge when we step outside inherited forms. The title suggests claiming ground, but for us, planting a hand is about testing whether something unfamiliar can take root at all.” I Plant My Hand in the Garden is produced by Maximilian Feldkamp for DFFB in Germany, with co-production by Taheri and Hadžija’s Cruising in Germany, Čarna Vučinić and Ena Bajraktarević for Naked in Serbia, and Tyler Hill for Mala Productions LLC in the U.S. Square Eyes is handling world sales. THR can exclusively premiere a trailer for the movie. We won’t spoil much beyond saying: get ready for wedding conversations, music, a lost condom – and talk of cake, among other things. full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All August 23, 2026 11:53pm Shashank Walia's 'Birds in the Dark' Courtesy of the Busan International Film Festival The Busan International Film Festival has unveiled 23 features for its Vision Korea and Vision Asia sections, filling out its showcase for Korean and Asian independent cinema ahead of the reveal of this year’s main competition slate. BIFF selected 12 films for Vision Korea and 11 for Vision Asia. The two strands were introduced last year, part of a broader overhaul that also saw Busan launch its first formal main competition section. The festival describes its Vision program as a showcase for new Korean and Asian independent cinema. The section grew out of Korean Cinema Today – Vision, which traditionally focused on emerging Korean filmmakers. When Busan expanded Visions’ remit to cover all of Asia, it also broadened the section to include mid-career directors alongside newcomers. Related Stories Movies Sandra Wollner's 'Everytime' Wins Best Film in Sarajevo, Ana Urushadze Crowned Best Director Movies 'Voice of Hind Rajab' Director Slams Israeli Military Investigation Into 5-Year-Old Girl's Death as a "Smokescreen" Among the Korean selections, Park Kun-young returns with Things I Left at the Theater , a drama about a film journalist searching for an old friend’s short film. Jang Woojin brings Cosmic Trace , centered on two people reflecting on love, loss, chance and fate at the boundary between life and death. Kim Miyoung, whose A Lonely Island in the Distant Sea won Busan’s DGK Megabox Award in 2023, is back with Some Detective , about a writer confronted by figures from her past. Both Some Detective and Shin Dongmin’s Not For You received post-production support from BIFF’s Asian Cinema Fund this year. (The full Visions lineup is below.) On the broader Asian side, Vietnamese filmmaker Nguyễn Hoàng Điệp returns with 1982 , about a bankrupt filmmaker searching for her missing mother and uncovering family secrets. Her first feature, Flapping in the Middle of Nowhere , premiered in Venice Critics’ Week in 2014 before screening at Busan. Filipino filmmaker Arvin Belarmino brings Ria , a folk-punk drama about a musician fighting to preserve her home and music, while Mongolia’s Sakhya Byamba, winner of Busan’s New Currents Award in 2013 for Remote Control , returns with Zogsool , a satire set around an isolated gas station during the early days of COVID-19. Thai actor Inthira Charoenpura makes her directing debut with Bua , co-directed by feature newcomer Phensiri Klangsurin. BIFF earlier named Kim Jong-kwan’s The Table: Day and Night as its 2026 opening film. The Seoul cafe-set romance, a loose follow-up to his 2016 feature The Table , will world premiere at the Busan Cinema Center on Oct. 6, with star Kim Minha hosting the opening ceremony. Michelle Yeoh will receive the Asian Filmmaker of the Year honor, Hong Kong auteur Ann Hui the Chanel-backed Camellia Award and festival founder Kim Dong-ho the Korean Cinema Award. The festival’s full competition lineup is still to come. BIFF will unveil its complete official selection in Seoul on Sept. 1 at its official opening press conference. title: ‘Game of Thrones’ Star Kristofer Hivju Turns to Rom-Com With ‘True Love’ by ‘Little Did I Know’s’ Martina Haag (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 23, 2026 11:30pm PT ‘Game of Thrones’ Star Kristofer Hivju Turns to Rom-Com With ‘True Love’ by ‘Little Did I Know’s’ Martina Haag (EXCLUSIVE) By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest Icelandic Producer Hlín Jóhannsdóttir Sets ‘Just a Kid’ With Alief Ahead of Haugesund and Reunites With ‘Driving Mum’ Team (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago Haugesund New Nordic Films Reveals Standout 36 Nordic Projects and 15 Fresh Pics Set to Woo 300 Industry Attendees 2 weeks ago Haugesund New Nordic Films Unveils French Focus Including a Case Study on ‘Ibelin,’ From ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum (EXCLUSIVE) 3 weeks ago See All From left, Helen Ahlsson, Kristofer Hivju and Martina Haag Credit: Courtesy of Anna-Lena Ahlström/SF Studios Norwegian star actor Kristofer Hivju (“Game of Thrones,” “ Red One ”, “Beck”) will play opposite Frida Hallgren (from Oscar-nominated “As It Is in Heaven”) in the upcoming Swedish-Croatian rom-com “True Love” (working title). Helmed by actor-turned writer, director and best-selling author Martina Haag , the SF Studios project, now in pre-production, will be pitched Aug. 26. at Haugesund’s Nordic Co-Production Market. Related Stories Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities LISTEN: Amazon Courts Creators to Build Businesses and Scale the Attention Economy for Brands “True Love” marks Haag’s second collaboration with seasoned screenwriter Peter Arrhenius (“Clark,” “Welcome to Sweden,” “Beck”) after the seasoned actor’s directorial debut “ Little Did I Know ,” which landed a Best Film Award at the Monte-Carlo Television Festival in 2024 before turning into one of Sweden’s biggest box office draws of 2025. Popular on Variety As with ‘ Little Did I know ,” “True Love”’s starting point is deceit and divorce and how to bounce back when you’re over 50. According to the logline, when Ellinor (played by Hallgren) is dumped by her husband after 20 years of marriage, she loses faith in life. When she wins €40 million ($46 million) immediately after, she finds it even harder to trust anyone. But then she meets Henrik (Hivju). The latter grew up at the elite Lundsberg boarding school, where his mother worked as a cleaner. To fit in, he learned to lie, and became an irresistibly charming master of deception. Their relationship should never work, but what if they’re exactly what the other needs? “As both main characters are flawed and a bit extreme in the beginning of the film, it was important for us to find great actors that are warm and relatable: Real people in exaggerated situations, that we want to be with and see get better,” said Hivju and Hallgren Haag. They added: “Both Frida and Kristofer feel grounded and are capable of going from being extremely funny to super sensitive. And of course, the chemistry and dynamics between the actors is super important in a romantic comedy. If the spark isn’t there, it doesn’t matter how great the story is. We’re so happy to have Frida and Kristofer on board!” Added SF Studios producer Helen Ahlsson : “Frida is a wonderfully warm and talented actress, and one audiences have taken to their hearts over the years. Kristofer has never really played a romantic lead before, which was perhaps a new challenge he was very keen to take on. In this film, you’ll discover a new Hivju like you’ve never seen before,” she enthusiastically shared with Variety . Haag said catering for mature audiences came naturally. “I love stories about and for women – and men – over 50,” she said. “I really can’t understand why we don’t see more of them as a whole scope of relatable, life altering relationship questions appear after surviving Project Family and raising the kids. One being deceit and divorce – as in “Little Did I Know” – but also how to be able to trust and love again.” “This story is about that,” she added. “Who we were, who we are, who we try to present ourself as, and who we really want to be. How can anyone dare to let their guard down and risk being hurt once again? We take that premise to the extreme in this film.” Teaming up again with Arrhenius was a no-brainer. “It is rare to find a writing partner that both has a skillset that completes your own and at the same time can respect and see your own strengths, like the yin and the yang,” she said, pointing out that “Peter is very interested in structure and serves up a lot of drastic jokes and situations, while I tend to focus on grounding these ideas in character and ”what would a real person do in this situation.” “When that works, what you get is drastic, funny situations happening to characters that feels true. Real emotions without being kitchen-sink drama. We share that desire to both touch an audience, but in an entertaining way,” she observed. Seasoned producer Ahlsson who’s worked mostly on dramas for film and TV – from Alicia Vikander’s Swedish debut “Pure” to Rojda Sekersöz’s upcoming “Will You Care if I Die” – said she couldn’t resist boarding her first rom-com after reading the script. “It’s got the magic of British comedy hits such as “Bridget Jones’s Diary” or “Mamma Mia,” which balance believable, engaging characters with lightness, humor and emotions. It’s a tricky mix that you can’t take lightly,” she said. Filming between Sweden-Stockholm, Dalecarlia-and Croatia is due to start Oct. 8, with delivery pencilled for fall 2027. The feature is produced by Scandi giant SF Studios in co-production with Croatia’s Kinorama, SVT and NRK, with funding from the Swedish Film Institute, Film Stockholm, Film i Dalarna, and a Croatian tax rebate. Ahlsson said she will discuss global sales at the New Nordic Films market unspooling Aug. 25-28 at Haugesund, Norway. Warner Bros. title: Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 23, 2026 11:16pm Paramount & Warner Bros water towers Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: A meeting Monday between Paramount brass and state Attorneys General over sussing out settlement talks between the parties in David Ellison ‘s contested $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery has turned into a “game of PR chicken,” an industry insider says. “Ellison and Makan Delrahim think they can force Rob Bonta into backing off with threats and intimidation,” a Tinseltown mandarin points out, as leaks out of Paramount insist the company is considering leaving California if the antitrust suit filed by the Golden State’s AG Bonta and 11 others ends up going to trial in March 2027. “That’s not going to work. He’s more determined that ever to take them to court, the rest is all for show, to take the pressure off.” Related Stories News Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo For "Antisemitism" & "Demonization" News Mark Ruffalo Blasts Paramount For Calling Him "Antisemitic" Over Merger Criticism: "Appalling And Fundamentally Dishonest" A part of that so-called show and responding to settlement calls from corporate and political stakeholders are some pretty audacious proposals that were discussed in August 21 communications between the AGs’ offices, their Milbank outside counsel, and the Melrose lot. Watch on Deadline It wasn’t quite the drama of Reagan and Gorbachev in Reykjavík in 1986, but there certainly were landmines. Setting the stage for the August 24 conference with promised “structural remedies,” Team AG are asking Paramount to sell off several of WBD’s cable channels. The Wall Street Journal first reported the potential conditions earlier Sunday. Doubting Ellison’s repeated promise to release 30 movies a year in cinemas is real or even possible, the states’ also want the movie studios kept separate, Deadline has confirmed. Bonta, New York’s Letitia James and the other blue state AGs have said they will bring a codicil of sort to the table for the August 24 huddle. In what is both a boss move and a poison pill, the AGs want Donald Trump’s “good friend” David Ellison agree to not have any day-to-day oversight or control of WB, I’m told. California Attorney General Rob Bonta left, Paramount CEO David Ellison Getty Images “David’s not going to go along with any of that, and Bonta knows it,” a studio exec told Deadline Sunday of stipulations that would neuter the mogul aspiring Para CEO and gut most of any immediate revenue streams for a $80 billion debt carrying ParaBros combo. Using terms like “performative” to describe Bonta and the other AGs staff agenda items, the exec asserts: “Ellison needs those cable channels, that’s still where the money is.” Though the object of much chatter and always in Trump’s bad books, sparkly CNN does not appear to be among the cable jewels the AGs want Oracle founder Larry Ellison’s son to divest himself of to get the merger done. HBO and HBO Max are not part of the talking points for the meeting, to no surprise. Individuals from different corners of the corporate, political and legal arena as well as with co-plaintiffs the Writers Guild of America, tell Deadline that expectations are “intentionally low” for that Monday’s meeting. “No one trusts anyone on the other side, it’s obvious,” the industry insider claims of the big law firms feeding frenzy, the big stakes and big personalities involved. “The states’ think Paramount’s going to say whatever they need to say to close the merger and avoid paying fees. Paramount think this is all partisan politics. Both sides are wrong and right, not willing to give anything big up. That’s not going to work if you want a deal.” While Paramount has made some minor M&A and ownership concessions outside the US and the UK for regulatory approval of the merger, the agenda items the AGs are throwing down are on a whole other level. A de facto obligation under the mediation proceedings routinely initiated in federal civil cases to prevent costly and time consuming trials, the perfunctory August 24 gathering took on exalted status in past 55 hours. After placed items that a Red State could become Para’s new HQ, and a tactical but punted Hail Mary request for the states to pony up a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the states’ case could cause home of The Godfather , increasingly lame duck Governor Gavin Newsom suddenly joined the chorus of exhibitors , gubernatorial candidates , the DGA, IATSE and flipping and then flopping again LA Mayor Karen Bass to break his Sphinx-like silence last week. Newsom said he believed “there’s some universal settlement there, if that’s possible” between his close colleague Bonta and his reported pal Ellison. Stressing on August 21 he took “seriously” the threats Paramount may leave California, the probable 2028 POTUS contender threw some Red media meat into the mix, adding: “I know there are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation.” Paramount had no comment Sunday on any proposals put forth late last week for discussion in Monday’s part face-to-face, part virtual meeting. The CA AG’s office, the NY AG’s office and the WGA did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment tonight. However, in what could be the first conversation between Ellison and Bonta since the AGs filed their now WGA joined antitrust action on July 13, there is hope on both sides that the principals can at least lower the temperature a tad. To that, Ellison may need to get much more directly involved Monday and going forward as a backlash is growing against Para’s chief legal officer and merger field marshal Delrahim. “It’s not just he says one thing in public, another in private,” a source close to events tells Deadline of the “frustrated” opinion officials have of the former Trump Assistant Attorney General and antitrust boss. “He seems to want to provoke a conflict for conflict’s sake.” Back in court, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin last week set August 26 as the date a Magistrate judge will be selected for mediation between Para and the AGs/WGA. An amended proposed scheduling order is due from the parties the same day. Besides leaks, tweets and the usual spin from the participant Monday, that order may prove to be the best indication what direction this all could really be going. title: Erik Poppe Talks Haugesund Opener ‘Beloved,’ Written by Nobel Prize Winner Jon Fosse: ‘People Long for Something Honest and Truthful’
full_text: Aug 23, 2026 11:15pm PT Erik Poppe Talks Haugesund Opener ‘Beloved,’ Written by Nobel Prize Winner Jon Fosse: ‘People Long for Something Honest and Truthful’ By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Erik Poppe Talks Haugesund Opener ‘Beloved,’ Written by Nobel Prize Winner Jon Fosse: ‘People Long for Something Honest and Truthful’ 4 hours ago ‘Sentimental Value’ Star Anders Danielsen Lie and Anne Marie Ottersen Inducted Into the Haugesund Walk of Fame: ‘It Feels Full Circle’ 18 hours ago Monica Bellucci Has ‘Never’ Done Anything Like ‘Ketticè’: ‘I Was on Set in My Pajamas With a Knife in My Hand and Slippers on My Feet’ 2 weeks ago See All Erik Poppe's 'Beloved' Courtesy of Reinvent Yellow Sales In “ Beloved ,” opening the Norwegian International Film Festival Haugesund , Erik Poppe takes on a script by Nobel Prize winner Jon Fosse. “It’s a project that has been on my desk for many, many years. Jon Fosse wrote it almost 20 years ago. After he received the Nobel Prize in Literature [in 2023], it felt like the whole world wanted to read it. But I always knew it was a powerful piece of work,” he tells Variety . Related Stories Ryan Murphy on Toning Down Sex in ‘The Shards’ and Why L.A. Mayor Karen Bass Could Do a ‘Much Better Job’ Bringing Productions Back to Hollywood 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story' Trailer: Ella Beatty Is an Axe Murderer in the Fourth Chapter of Ryan Murphy's Bloody Anthology Series “Beloved” follows a couple who meet in a small coastal town. They have a child, but Asle is drawn back to the sea while Gerd remains in the village. Popular on Variety The film, starring Leo Magnus de la Nuez and Kristi-Helene Giæver Engeberg, was produced by Paradox and SF Production. It’s sold by Reinvent Yellow Sales. One of Norway’s most acclaimed directors, Poppe is known for larger productions, from “The King’s Choice” to “Utøya: July 22,” “The Emigrants” and “Quisling: The Final Days.” But focusing on a more intimate story felt right this time. “Looking at the world as it is right now, I needed to hold onto some sense of hope – or at least something more human. I wanted to explore the relationship between two people, as well as between a father and son, because it’s a story of daily life I can relate to.” He adds: “We’ve all seen how well they perform in the cinemas, surprisingly enough. People long for something honest and truthful that they can just dive into.” The fact that Fosse is only growing in stature doesn’t hurt either. “He’s about to be named one of the most important living authors in the world today, and this isn’t based on his novels or plays. [The screenplay] is an original piece of work that he wrote with only one goal in mind: to make it into a movie.” Still more adaptations are likely on their way. “I’m quite sure more movies will be made from his novels. As a filmmaker, he’s opening up the space between the dialogue for me to fill in. His style is so simple yet deep. You connect with it, understand it, and it hits you right in the stomach. His novels are short, but when you read them, it feels like Dostoyevsky. I find it extraordinary.” Despite following only two characters and their son, Poppe didn’t change his approach to working with actors. “On all my movies, I insist on having at least eight or 12 weeks with them [prior to the shoot]. If I can establish a truthful, honest relationship with my actors, I can push them quite far,” he says. He also paid extra attention to their surroundings. “I spent a lot of time figuring out where to shoot this film. It’s almost like a mythical landscape, a mythical part of Norway. It’s the fourth character in the film.” Misty and melancholic, it mirrors their insecurities and growing estrangement. “It’s quite typical of many relationships. It’s so hard to talk to each other,” says Poppe. “I was raised by two parents who were almost exactly like these two. Except, it was my mother who left and my sister and I stayed home with my father. The film is about the language these two used to share, which is disappearing, it’s about where they are and what they’re longing for.” Which is why, despite that title, there is a darker side to ‘Beloved.’ “Based on our first screenings, people have been surprised, but they also really love that it’s not your regular love story,” he admits. “I think it’s a brave piece of work by Jon. I was tempted by the fact that he doesn’t follow the paths we are so used to. I wanted to explore how that could work in a movie.” ‘American Blue’ Pilot With Milo Ventimiglia Not Moving Forward at HBO Max Paula Reid, CNN’s Chief Legal Affairs Correspondent, Will Exit Ahead of Paramount Takeover HBO Max Leads the Emmy Drama and Comedy Races for the First Time Since 2017. title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Outmuscles ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to Hold Top Spot
full_text: Aug 23, 2026 11:01pm PT Korea Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Outmuscles ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to Hold Top Spot By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Alia Bhatt’s Young-Adult Rom-Com ‘Don’t Be Shy’ Sets September Prime Video Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) 60 minutes ago ‘An Oak Tree’ Casts Sacha Dhawan, Gemma Whelan for London Run (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago ‘Emomee,’ Indian Kids Life-Skills Series, Lands on Netflix (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Everett Collection “ The Odyssey ” maintained its commanding position atop the South Korea box office during the weekend of Aug. 21–23. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Christopher Nolan-directed tentpole generated $10.6 million from 1,321,204 admissions over the three-day frame across 2,182 screens, capturing 66.3% of total weekend business. Showing formidable holding power in its third outing, the film pushed its cumulative local gross to $56.8 million from 7,109,368 total admissions since its Aug. 5 launch. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, the franchise installment has reached a total of $2.5 million from 356,276 tickets. The local action-comedy sequel “Ok! Madam: Bon Voyage” took sixth place, generating $239,231 from 33,585 admissions. Directed by Lee Cheol-ha and starring Uhm Jung-hwa, Park Sung-woong, Lee Sang-yun, and Sooyoung, the film has now earned $2 million. “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” placed seventh, collecting $143,937 from 20,488 admissions to move its gross to $671,567 from 95,605 admissions. title: John Oliver Takes a Close Look at Sean Duffy’s “God-Awful” New Reality Show: “We’ve All Been Taken for a F***ing Ride”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All August 23, 2026 9:47pm 'Last Week Tonight With John Oliver' Courtesy of HBO John Oliver took a close look at what he called a “less-covered story from this week” on Sunday’s Last Week Tonight : a reality show from U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy called The Great American Road Trip. Duffy debuted a trailer for the show in May. At the time, a press release stated that the series “asks: Who are we? Following U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and his family, this five-part journey encourages Americans to step away from their screens for a vital civic experience. From small towns to iconic landmarks, the series captures the unscripted moments and shared values that prove to love America, you have to see America. The series will be released for free on YouTube, allowing every American family to follow along.” The show was timed to debut during this year, the nation’s 250th anniversary. Related Stories News Did Alex Vindman Just Get Burned by the Larry David Curse? Lifestyle Abdul El-Sayed's Watch Collection Has Drawn Scrutiny -- Is It Luxury or Simply Geek Chic? “So the motto is to love America is to see America,” Duffy explains to President Donald Trump in the trailer. He continues in voice-over: “It’s more than a road trip. It’s a civic experience. It’s one of the most powerful ways to understand the vast, beautiful, complicated place we call home.” (Watch it below.) Said Oliver of the trailer: “OK, lots not to like there — from the generic ‘hey ho’ folk rock to Trump giving insane grandma’s new boyfriend vibes to the very conspicuous close up of the Toyota logo to the seemingly AI-generated images of cars, which makes sense. No one’s ever thought to film a real car before.” At the time the show was announced, Duffy’s wife, Fox News Channel host Rachel Campos Duffy, “even claimed it was a solution to what ails us as a nation,” Oliver said. “I’m going to be really honest, we live in a Pornhub world,” Rachel said in a Fox News clip shown by Oliver. “This is really wholesome, good family stuff. This is what families need to do is just get together. That’s what our kids want from us.” Replied Oliver: “Is it? Because I think what every kid really wants is for their mum not to say the word ‘Pornhub’ on national TV. Also, she clearly hasn’t spent a lot of time on that site, or she’d know, families getting together is very much its own category.” However, the road-trip series drew controversy for a few reasons: the high cost of gas, the fact that Sean was out filming a reality series when he had an important government job to do, and who was paying for the show. Regarding the latter, Sean said that it wasn’t funded by taxpayer money; instead the series was funded through a nonprofit production company called Great American Road Trip Inc. However, that organization’s website lists 17 sponsors, many of which are companies that the Department of Transportation oversees and regulates. “Yeah, that’s not great,” said Oliver. “The only worse answer to who pay for this than ‘the American taxpayer’ is ‘a bunch of companies I oversee and regulate.’ Actually, I suppose an even worse answer would be a bunch of companies I oversee and regulate, and also my close personal friend Jeffrey Epstein.” The show was supposed to be released in June, but “all the scrutiny seemed to delay it,” Oliver noted, and all six episodes were “quietly dumped on YouTube” last week. Oliver said that it’s no surprise that Sean, a former star of MTV’s The Real World : Boston , wanted to return to reality TV. (He also met his wife on Road Rules: All Stars .) But Oliver pointed out some discrepancies in how Duffy recalled his time on those shows over the years. For example, in Road Trip, he visits the house that the Real World: Boston cast stayed in while filming and “tries to rewrite some history,” the Last Week Tonight host said. During the segment, Sean reflects on the tension between him and housemate Kameelah Phillips, denying he called her a “bitch.” But Oliver showed a clip from The Real World in which Duffy says, “I walked up ahead of the group and I called her a bitch.” “You did call her that,” Oliver said. “Call me CVS, Sean, because I will always bring the receipts.” As for Sean’s claim that the show is “a nationwide storytelling movement that invites Americans to explore the open road, connect with their communities,” Oliver said, “That’s not really what it is at all, because it turns out it’s basically just an expensively produced test run of a Duffy family reality show with each episode featuring a bare minimum about travel or America, but a ton of manufactured reality TV drama around the Duffys doing stuff like planning a family party or over the course of several episodes watching their daughter decide which college she’ll attend.” As for that lattter point, Sean and Rachel are seen talking to their daughter about her desire to go to Harvard, which they evidently don’t support because they believe Harvard has “professionalized figuring out how they can take good young girls like you and I think corrupt their minds,” Sean tells his daughter in the show while the two are chatting in their kitchen. Replied Oliver: “What the fuck are you talking about? First, this was supposed to be a road trip. Why are we still in your kitchen? Second, is there anything less relatable than a family whose conflict is, how do I tell my daughter she can’t go to Harvard because we did too good a job raising her?” He continued: “And finally, please don’t be worried that Harvard’s going to corrupt your daughter’s mind. Be worried that if she goes there, like every other Harvard grad, she’s never gonna shut the fuck up about it. One of this show’s writers went to Harvard and guess how I know that? Exactly . I don’t know where any of the others went.” Oliver then said that it’s no surprise that “hardly anyone” seems to have watched the show, based on the number of viewers available on YouTube. It also received very little promotion. “I don’t really give a shit if Sean Duffy and his wife want to become the next Duggars or Jon and Kate [Gosselin] or Alec and Hilaria Baldwin,” Oliver said, citing other families who’ve starred in reality TV shows. “What’s concerning is them doing it on the back of the Department of Transportation because it feels ethically dubious on so many levels, which may be why at this point everyone involved in The Great American Road Trip seems like they’d rather just sweep it under the rug.” He continued: “[H]aving watched all three hours of this god-awful show, from gender reveals to the Duffys renewing their vows for no clear reason, it feels less like the country’s been taken on a road trip by Sean Duffy and a lot more like we’ve all been taken for a fucking ride.” THR

title: Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 23, 2026 8:04pm (L-R) Mark Curry, Raquel Lee, Dawnn Lewis, Tahj Mowry in 2001's The Proof Point Disney The Proof Point’ s Raquel Lee claims in a extremely graphic negligence suit against the Walt Disney Company she was “repeatedly raped, sexually assaulted, sexually abused and sexually harassed” on the Utah set of the 2001 movie. The House of Mouse knew about it and did nothing to stop the violence, the Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV participant adds. “John Doe (“Mr. Doe”), an on-set, adult, middle-aged, male employee of Disney who was involved in the filming of the movie,” the August 21 filing in LA Superior Court for the now Raquel Lee Boileau from NYC-based Wigdor LLP says with intentional vagueness about the alleged predator. “Mr. Doe’s sexual abuse of Ms. Boileau was apparent to the adults on Disney’s set. Defendant Disney repeatedly failed Ms. Boileau. Disney facilitated and concealed Mr. Doe’s severe sexual abuse of Ms. Boileau.” Related Stories News 'National Treasure 3' In Works, Franchise Director Reveals: "It's Finally Real" News Disney Inks Creator Content Deal With Dhar Mann Studios “Disney’s set was not safe for children,” the unspecified “money judgement” seeking complaint states of what the 14-year-old Lee faced on the Mark Curry-led and Neal Israel-directed Disney Channel film. A case of kooky scientists ( Hangin With Mr Copper’s Curry and Dawnn Lewis) their kids (Lee and Tahj Mowry), the time traveling Proof Point debuted on September 14, 2001. Watch on Deadline Claiming the “visibly disheveled” teen was also at the receiving end of tirades from Disney execs at the time over her performance, the filing strategically invokes the much accused, much convicted and Incarcerated Harvey Weinstein , among others. With the ex-Miramax kingpin in mind, the now nearly 40-year-old actress’ jury trial desiring filing adds: “This is not the first time that Disney has enabled a sexual predator to target and abuse vulnerable victims. Disney has a longstanding and horrifying history of protecting sexual abusers that began well before 2001-and continued after 2001.” “Disney has caused irreparable and devastating harm, and must be held accountable,” the action claims for its client. “Defendant failed to use reasonable care in investigating the circumstances on set and did nothing to reasonably investigate, supervise or monitor and/or terminate Mr. Doe to ensure the safety of child actors,” it also bluntly says. Contacted by Deadline, Disney today had no comment on the suit or the accusations within it. That’s not surprising all things litigious considered – even more so with the amount of time that has passed and people involved who are no longer at Disney. In terms of a situation specific timeline, the first the Josh D’Aamaro-led company heard about this sordid case was back in June, sources say. That was when Doug Wigdor and Jame Kim approached Disney in the hopes of settling this out of court. Clearly, the parties couldn’t reach a satisfactory deal. What is also clear is that while Disney may or may not have first heard of the horrors Lee went through in 2001 just a few months ago, this four-claim action is not the first time the actress has had lawyers involved fallout from Poof Point . Deadline has learned that in 2015 a Gloria Allred -represented Lee negotiated a confidential settlement for “a small amount of money” with a male who worked on Proof Point. The male in question was represented by Venable partner William Biggs, II. Allred had no comment on any settlement or anything to do with it when contacted by Deadline. Biggs did not response to Deadline’s request for comment on that matter of over a decade ago. Details of that settlement and the exact sum paid out are under lock and key – – hence likely the “John Doe “in this new civil complaint. However, the presence of Allred, well known for her work for sexual assault survivors, could be an indication of the nature of the core case back in 2015. As for this latest action, the law has changed in Lee’s favor. Whereas in the past Lee would have long exhausted the statute of limitations, under a 2020 California measure, survivors of childhood sexual abuse now have up until their 40th birthday to file a civil claim. Actually, an 2023 addition to that 2020 law removed any statute of limitations for civil claims of childhood sexual assault survivors that occurred on or after January 1, 2024. Under the law as it stands now, a plaintiff can claims triple actual damages if it is proven a company (like Disney), institution or persons(s) were aware of the assaults and abuse and choose to conceal what was happening. A state of affairs that is precisely what Lee is saying Disney did in her case on Poof Point. It is worth noting that former Real Husbands of Hollywood regular Raquel Lee Boileau has worked with Disney on several occasions since The Poof Point . She did voiceover on Disney+’s The Proud Family: Louder and Proude r . Debuting in 2022, the animated series was a revival of Disney Channel’s The Proud Family , which Raquel Lee Boileau was also on from 2001-2005. Raquel Lee Boileau’s attorneys had nothing to say whatsoever today on any 2015 settlement, but they were not silent about what they filed this weekend. “Over the last decade, countless child actors have come forward to bravely share their experiences of abuse by adults in entertainment,” said Doug Wigdor and Jane Kim. “As former government prosecutors, our message to the entertainment industry is simple: This conduct is inexcusable, and those involved—directly or indirectly—must be held accountable.” It is also worth noting Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV’s Broadcast Arm Sony’s One-Two Punch: $39M For ‘Spider-Man’ & $25M+ For ‘Insidious’ Settlement Talks With State AGs This Week; Newsom Weighs In On Merger Karoline Leavitt Reveals Post-White House Press Secretary Job Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Vultures’ Swoops To Top Award At Oscar-Qualifying HollyShorts Film Festival (Full Winners List)
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew HollyShorts Festival Set To Propel Documentary Jury Award Winner Into Oscar Race Doc Talk Podcast: Rebecca Miller On Her Emmy-Nominated ‘Mr. Scorsese’, A Journey Into The Mind And Mastery Of Martin Scorsese DOC NYC Set To Honor Documentary Visionaries Alex Gibney, JT Takagi, Stephen Maing, And Raney Aronson-Rath View All August 23, 2026 6:32pm HollyShorts Dian Weys’ drama Vultures clutched top honors at HollyShorts Sunday evening, winning the prestigious festival’s Grand Jury Prize for Best Short Film. The award qualifies the film for Oscar consideration and comes with a prize of a $60,000 Panavision camera package. Edwin van der Walt, Jill Levenberg, and Albert Pretorius star in the 15-minute-long short from the South African-born filmmaker. Logline: “In the volatile moments after a car crash, before the authorities arrive, a hot-headed yet desperate tow truck driver fiercely protects his tow. But the situation quickly spirals out of his control.” Related Stories Documentary HollyShorts Festival Set To Propel Documentary Jury Award Winner Into Oscar Race News 'Degree of Certainty' Filmmaker Simon Schneider Tackles The Ironic Origins Of Climate Change Data -- HollyShorts Film Festival ‘Vultures’ HollyShorts Vultures also won the festival’s Best International award. The film premiered at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival and has screened around the world since then, including at Tribeca Festival, the Red Sea International Film Festival in Saudi Arabia, and the Zagreb Film Festival in Croatia. Weys’ previous credits include the shorts Bergie (2022) and Versnel (2017), and the 50-minute-long thriller Koffie en Sigarette (2023). Watch on Deadline In addition to the Panavision package, the Grand Jury Prize for Best Short Film comes with three hours of complimentary legal consultation presented by Sheppard Mullin. Along with the Grand Jury Prize, HollyShorts is Oscar-qualifying in three additional shorts categories: Best Live Action, Best Animation, and Best Documentary. HollyShorts The Best Live Action Award was claimed by Pale Sun , directed by Adrian Moyse Dullin and Jawahine Zentar. Anass El Hmami, Baki Bousmaha, and Sylvie Fasano star in that film, the story of 12-year-old Abel, who while spending time on a beach in summer with his family finds himself “ashamed of his father’s body, marked by cancer.” HollyShorts Best Animation went to With Tapes and Toasts in the Car (Im Auto Tapes und Butterbrot) , directed by Kiana Naghshineh. Logline: “In the face of her body fading into stardust, Shari realizes what truly matters to her.” Naghshineh, a native of Mannheim, Germany, studied animation at the Filmakademie Baden – Württemberg. Her previous films incude Augenblicke (2018) and Don Pasquale (2018). Aspen Film The Time My Grandmother Was Held Hostage by Bank Robbers , directed by Rosella Tursi, won the Best Documentary jury award. The film’s title gives a very strong sense of the content: the director’s nonna (Italian for grandmother) was held hostage in her home in Montreal in 1983 after two men fleeing a bank holdup entered her dwelling through an open door. Archive footage shows how news crews descended on the home as the hostage drama unfolded. The documentary is built around memories of that day shared by members of nonna Rosa’s family, as well as recollections from one of the bank robbers/hostage takers himself – a man tracked down by filmmaker Rosella Tursi over 40 years after the crime. (I served on the jury in this category). The awards ceremony was held at the TCL Chinese Theatres at Ovation Hollywood. Scroll for the full list of winners for the 22 nd edition of HollyShorts. Russell Tovey in ‘I Am the Prize.’ Courtesy I Am the Prize New this year at HollyShorts is the Best Performance Award, recognizing outstanding acting in short-form filmmaking.
